data.name: Khusrow
data.gender_notes: Khusrow is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word ‘Khud’, meaning 'self'. Khusrow refers to a ruler or king who has power over the world. The name Khusrow carries the meaning “Ruler of the World” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khusrow usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the world and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Khusrow belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler of the World.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khusrow total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: خوسرو
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من الفارسية يعني الملك أو الحاكم
in_arabic.long_meaning: خوسرو هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل فارسي، يعني الملك أو الحاكم، ويرجع إلى عصر الإمبراطورية الساسانية. وقد ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنبياء، الآية 78، حيث ذكر اسم الملك خوسرو بن سابور بن أردشير. ويعتبر هذا الاسم من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني القوة والسلطة في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: خوسرو
in_urdu.meaning: فارسی سے ماخوذ اسم، معنی بادشاہ یا حاکم
in_urdu.long_meaning: خوسرو ایک فارسی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے بادشاہ یا حاکم۔ یہ نام ساسانی سلطنت کے دور سے منسلک ہے۔ اردو زبان میں، یہ نام مذہبی اور ثقافتی لحاظ سے اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے، خاص طور پر مسلم اشرافیہ میں۔

in_hindi.name: खुसरो
in_hindi.meaning: फ़ारसी से लिया गया नाम, अर्थ राजा या शासक
in_hindi.long_meaning: खुसरो फ़ारसी भाषा से लिया गया एक नाम है, जिसका अर्थ है राजा या शासक। यह नाम सासानी साम्राज्य के समय से जुड़ा हुआ है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम ऐतिहासिक और सांस्कृतिक महत्व रखता है।

in_pashto.name: خوسرو
in_pashto.meaning: د فارس څخه اخیستل شوی نوم، معنی پاچا یا واکمن
in_pashto.long_meaning: خوسرو د فارس څخه اخیستل شوی نوم دی، چې معنی یې پاچا یا واکمن دی. دا نوم د ساساني سترواکمنۍ دورې پورې تړاو لري. په پښتني کلتور کې، دا نوم د ځواک او واکمنۍ نښه ګڼل کېږي.

in_english.name: Khusrow
in_english.meaning: Derived from Persian, meaning king or ruler
in_english.long_meaning: Khusrow is a name derived from Persian roots, signifying a king or ruler. It has etymological connections to the Sasanian Empire era. In Islamic tradition, the name is associated with strength, authority, and leadership. Historically, Khusrow has been borne by several notable figures, including Persian kings and nobles. The name carries a sense of grandeur and dignity, reflecting its origins in royal and imperial contexts.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic literature and mythology, Khusrow is a renowned character prominent in various romantic and tragic tales. He represents a powerful and just ruler, cherished by his people, who falls deeply in love and subsequently experiences heartache and sorrow. Khusrow's story exemplifies the complex relationship between rulers and their subjects, as well as the power and consequences of love in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Khusrow symbolizes the inner struggle of the self towards achieving perfection and power, while remaining compassionate, just, and true. He challenges us to acknowledge the power within ourselves, to rule our desires and impulses with wisdom and kind-heartedness, and to strike a balance between worldly duty and spiritual growth. Furthermore, Khusrow's tragic love story serves as a reminder of the transient nature of material possessions as well as the importance of maintaining peace, forgiveness, and unity in our relationships.

historical_references.reference: Khusrow I Anushirvan, the Sassanian emperor who ruled from 531 to 579 AD, was known for his religious tolerance and promotion of Zoroastrianism and Manicheanism. He is often considered as the last great emperor of the Sassanian Empire.
historical_references.context: Sassanian Empire, religious tolerance, Zoroastrianism, Manicheanism

historical_references.reference: Khusrow II, also known as Chosroes II, was a Sassanian king who ruled from 590 to 628 AD. He faced numerous military challenges from the Byzantine Empire and internal rebellions. Khusrow II is most famous for ordering the construction of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, which is considered the first Islamic mosque built outside the Arabian Peninsula.
historical_references.context: Sassanian Empire, Byzantine Empire, internal rebellions, Dome of the Rock

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Khusrow' is of Persian origin and is associated with the legendary king of the Sassanid Empire, Khusrow Anushirvan. In modern context, 'Khusrow' is often referenced in various fields. In literature, it's a popular character in Persian literature and historical fiction. In Goodreads and Amazon Kindle, you can find numerous books featuring this king. In gaming, 'Khusrow' is a character or faction name in popular games like 'Assassin's Creed: Valhalla', 'Total War: Three Kingdoms', and 'Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord'. These platforms reflect the enduring interest in the history, culture, and mythology of ancient Persia.
